evidence.field: 形義通解; oracle-bone forms and readings
evidence.text: The entry reports two major early analyses: 日+月 interpreted either as dawn, with the sun rising before the moon sets, or as brightness; and 月+囧 interpreted as moonlight through a perforated window, with 囧 also proposed as a sound element. It reports 目+月 examples as too fragmentary to identify securely and 田+月 as possibly a corruption of 日 or 囧. The database cites oracle-bone examples for dawn in 合集481 (乙巳明雨) and brightness in 合集21037 (不喪朙), but their relative chronology is not established.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 明

evidence.text: The entry reports bronze uses for dawn in 大盂鼎 and later senses including clear, manifest, and morally upright in bronze inscriptions. These listed examples do not by themselves establish a semantic chronology or the path from dawn/brightness to clear or manifest.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 明

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: 說文釋形; 字樣說明; 釋義
evidence.text: The dictionary states that Shuowen's standard seal form is 朙, analyzed as 月 plus 囧, with gloss 照也 (‘illuminate’); it identifies a 日/月 form as the ancient-script form. It quotes the Shijing line 東方明矣，朝既昌矣 as an example of daybreak, but this historical account does not establish which sense came first.
evidence.title: A01784 明 — Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: 異體字研訂; 漢語拼音
evidence.text: The entry identifies 朙 as a variant of 明 and gives its Mandarin reading míng. Its quotation of Shuowen treats 明 as the ancient form of 朙. These claims concern the historical dictionary account and variant relationship, not proof that 朙 was the only early graphic construction.
evidence.title: A01784 明 — Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: 說文釋形; 漢語拼音
evidence.text: The entry gives modern Mandarin jiǒng for 囧 and records Shuowen's 讀若獷 alongside Jia Shi Zhong's report 讀與明同. These are historical pronunciation statements; they do not independently recover the spoken name of the depicted window or demonstrate a phonetic correspondence in 朙.
evidence.title: B00484 囧 — Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.field: 漢字甲骨部件分析; 囧
evidence.text: The entry describes 囧 as a perforated window and cites a separate oracle-bone use as a place name (合集10, 黍于囧). It quotes Shuowen's differing pronunciation notices, 讀若獷 and Jia Shi Zhong's 讀與明同. This supports that historical lexicographers recorded competing pronunciation views; the window's original spoken name is not established here.

evidence.field: 字形演變; 圖形說明
evidence.text: The character record groups 明 forms under oracle-bone, bronze, Chu manuscript, small-seal, and Shuowen ancient-script headings, including a bronze example indexed as 集成00161. It presents the 日+月 explanation for brightness. This account supports one early analysis but does not establish it as the sole early construction.
